name: python-package-identity
body:
A Python source file's module identity must follow Python's package model and stay collision-free. A directory containing __init__.py or __init__.pyi is a package; a module's dotted identity is built by walking up its ancestors while they are init-bearing packages; a file with no init-bearing ancestor is a flat top-level module. The frontend emits one Module node per discovered package/module and sets each File's parent to its module, so the ingestor's `parent.name` rendering yields the dotted symbol FQNs.

The shared Module FQN namespace also carries language/package-derived names from other frontends (a Cargo package name, an npm package name, a Go module path), so collision-freedom across the whole scan must hold. DECIDED (reconciled with the language-rooting decision): the rendered Python Module FQN is the language-rooted form `py.<dotted-identity>` — the language-namespaced form. The `py` root is disjoint from every other language's root and from markdown's rooted absolute paths, so a root Python package `apg` renders `py.apg`, never colliding with the Rust `rust.apg` module, and two same-stem init-less top-level modules in different directories resolve by their distinct dotted identities. The former open design point (bare dotted vs path-derived vs language-namespaced) is closed: requirements.note.python-frontend-open-points #1 is DECIDED. Discovery must not descend into generated/dependency trees (see domain.constraint.python-exclusions).

AC: a package pkg/ with __init__.py and pkg/sub/__init__.py yields two distinct module nodes rendered `py.pkg` and `py.pkg.sub`, each containing its files' symbols; a directory with no __init__.py yields a distinct flat module node rendered `py.<stem>`; no two discovered modules render to the same FQN and the scan triggers no ingestor FQN-collision panic.
